title: indirect enum: Expression Trees
hints: A recursive enum needs `indirect` so its cases can contain the enum.
Parse RPN with a stack of `Expr`: numbers push, operators pop two (or one for `neg`) and push the combined node.
`guard let b = stack.popLast(), let a = stack.popLast() else { return nil }; stack.append(.add(a, b))`.
jsBridge: `indirect enum Expr` is a recursive discriminated union (an AST), like TS `type Expr = {k:'num',v:number} | {k:'add',l:Expr,r:Expr}`. `indirect` boxes the recursive cases so the enum has a finite size.

compass.q: TS recursive union types need no `indirect`. Why does Swift need it (value types have a fixed size)?
Indirect enum AST vs class hierarchy AST: which makes adding a new *operation* (pretty-print) easier?
Can you mark only some cases `indirect`? What's the memory difference?
Where do trees appear in apps: JSON, Markdown, view hierarchies, rich-text documents?
